senses.definition: The process of doing something.
examples: He was caught in the act of stealing.

senses.definition: (countable) A formal or official record of something done.
(countable, drama) A division of a theatrical performance.
examples: The pivotal moment in the play was in the first scene of the second act.

quotes.text: “H'm !” he said, “so, so—it is a tragedy in a prologue and three acts. senses.definition: (countable) A performer or performers in a show.
examples: Which act did you prefer? The soloist or the band?

examples: If you don’t act soon, you will be in trouble.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To perform a theatrical role.
examples: I started acting at the age of eleven in my local theatre.

senses.definition: (intransitive) Of a play: to be acted out (well or badly).

quotes.text: But whatever types he assumes, the need to have a good play which acts delightfully well before the audience, and to their delectation, is the dominant thrust. If the play acts well, the director gets the credits.
quotes.reference: 2011, Effiong Johnson, Play Production Processes, page 180:

senses.definition: (intransitive) To behave in a certain manner for an indefinite length of time.
examples: A dog which acts aggressively is likely to bite.
I believe that Bill’s stuck-up because of the way that he acts.
He’s acting strangely—I think there’s something wrong with him.

senses.definition: (copulative) To convey an appearance of being.
examples: He acted unconcerned so the others wouldn’t worry.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To do something that causes a change binding on the doer.
(intransitive, construed with on or upon) To have an effect (on).
examples: High-pressure oxygen acts on the central nervous system and may cause convulsions or death.
Gravitational force acts on heavy bodies.

senses.definition: (transitive) To play (a role).
examples: He’s been acting Shakespearean leads since he was twelve.

senses.definition: (transitive) To feign.
examples: He acted the angry parent, but was secretly amused.

quotes.text: With acted fear the villain thus pursued.
quotes.reference: 1697, Virgil, “The Second Book of the Æneis”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London: […] Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:

senses.definition: (intransitive, law) To carry out work as a legal representative in relation to a particular legal matter.
examples: A lawyer cannot act until they have been formally instructed by their client.

senses.definition: (intransitive, mathematics, construed with on or upon, of an algebraic structure) To possess an action onto (some other structure). Examples include the group action of a group on a set, the action of a ring on a module by scalar multiplication, and the action of a group or algebra on a vector space via a representation.
examples: This group acts on the circle, so it can't be left-orderable!

senses.definition: (obsolete, transitive) To move to action; to actuate; to animate.

quotes.text: Self-love, the spring of motion, acts the soul.
